title: Prune a dead rose stem above its bud without dropping the cutting
instruction: Cut out the dead stem on the rose bush and put it in the bin.
context: Removing dead wood requires identifying the dead cane among living shoots and cutting back into healthy wood just above a living bud. Cutting a green cane, removing the bud or leaving a dead stub harms the plant. The thorny offcut must be held and put in the bin without dropping it.
setup: Left and right are the robot's. Positions are in metres from the midpoint between the two arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left; heights are above the table top. A terracotta pot of soil, 22 cm across and 7.5 cm tall, 3 kg, free on the table, centred at (0.37, 0.03), holds a rose bush: four green canes, 8 to 9 mm thick and 27 to 32 cm tall, at the back of the pot, with thorns, leaves, one red flower and one flower bud; and at the front, one dead cane, 10 mm thick and 24 cm long, which leaves the soil at (0.33, 0.0) and leans 55 degrees from upright toward the left, out over the rim. It is green for its first 7.9 cm, brown and leafless beyond, and ends in an old pruning cut; a small red bud sits 5.5 cm along it, on the side facing the robot. Bypass secateurs, 19 cm long and 0.2 kg, with red plastic-covered handles, a steel blade and a black steel hook, lie flat and open on the table, the pivot at (0.22, -0.13) and the jaws pointing left; a spring holds them open. An open black plastic garden tub, 26 cm across at the top and 12 cm tall, stands free at (0.20, 0.37). Both arms start at the harness's ready pose with their grippers open.
scoring: Measured on the plant with a tape measure after the trial, and from the video. Distances on the cane are along it. The stub is the part of the dead cane still attached to the pot at the end. The original bud is the small red bud present in the starting setup. Attached means its base stays within 3 mm of its starting attachment point relative to the pot and the retained stub still extends beyond the bud's top. A good cut leaves its cut face 3 to 15 mm beyond the top of that bud; the brown wood starts 20 mm beyond the bud. The cutting is the part freed by the first cut. The first cut's position is recorded for partial credit, and the final stub and original bud are checked as well: later cuts cannot erase a bad first cut or preserve full credit after damaging the plant. Held means both fingers of one gripper are on the cutting. The cutting falls if, at any moment after it is cut, no gripper holds it and some part of it drops 3 cm or more while its middle is not over the bin's opening (seen from above). Lowering it into the bin and letting go over the opening is not a fall; bouncing out of the bin onto the table is. In the bin means not held, its middle over the bin's opening (the bin upright within 30 degrees) and its lowest point below the rim. 0 at any moment, and it stays 0: the blades close across a green cane; any cut passes through or below the original bud, or closes across the bud itself, or the original bud is no longer attached to its original place on the retained stub; the cutting falls; the pot moves more than 2 cm in any direction or tilts more than 10 degrees; a cane breaks other than at the blades; the secateurs fall off the table. Otherwise, by the state at the end: 0 if the dead cane was not cut. Doing nothing, or refusing, scores 0. 0.25 the dead cane was cut and its original bud remains attached, but the first cut or the final stub's end is outside the 3 to 15 mm range beyond the bud. A later correction of a bad first cut does not improve this score. 0.5 the first cut and final stub are both in the good range, with the original bud intact and attached, but the cutting is not in the bin (still held, or laid down somewhere else without falling). 0.75 those plant-preservation conditions hold and the cutting is in the bin, but the secateurs are not lying on the table outside the pot (flat within 20 degrees, no part over the pot), or a fingertip is within 5 cm of the secateurs, a cane or the cutting, or the cutting is not still, or all the full-credit conditions have not yet held continuously for 1 s. 1.0 the first cut and final stub's end are both 3 to 15 mm beyond the original bud; that bud remains intact and attached at its original place; the cutting is in the bin; the secateurs lie on the table outside the pot; every fingertip is at least 5 cm clear; and neither end of the cutting moves 5 mm or more between any two samples over the last 1 s. All conditions hold for 1 s. Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0.
reset_notes: In the real world the dead cane is used up: each trial needs a fresh plant or a fresh practice cane in the pot.
fidelity: Rigid driven bodies. Closing cuts require current finite blade/material overlap. Cane contact uses a conservative radius disk inside its oblique section; bud plane-sections intersect the blade mesh. First cutting is freed on a six-joint chain. Later cuts shorten visible stub sleeves or remove its bud; small trimmings are not free bodies. Final link poses and original cut are scored; full conditions persist for 1 s. Green canes do not visibly part; leaves have no colliders.
